messages:
oncall-bot: INCIDENT ALERT: GPU pool eu-west-1-gpu-pool-12 capacity-critical -> paging oncall (SLO impact, queue growth). Autoescalate policy: page @olivia and @jamal.

oncall-bot: Pager: 3x critical alerts in 5m: queue length > 12k, throttle rate 78%, node count collapsed -2 in last 10m.

Olivia Chen: ack-ing. jumping in. initial read: autoscaler tried to add GPUs but nodes flapped, lots of CUDA/Xid on the tail.

Maya Patel: seeing repeated Xid: 704 errors and OOMs on driver. logs:```
2026-03-15T22:02:17Z driver.c:WARN GPU0: Xid 704 on app pid=4821
2026-03-15T22:02:18Z runtime:OOM: process gservec: alloc 2048MB failed
2026-03-15T22:02:19Z kubelet: Evicting pod job-embedding-43 (OOM)
```

Jamal Singh: autoscaler metrics: currentReplicas=24, desiredReplicas=38, maxReplicas=40, but failed scale attempts: 7/7 in last 8m. Error from cloud: "instanceLaunchFailed: driver-init-timeout". Looks like nodes start but driver module crashes on init -> pool not registering.

Evan (ML Infra): customer-facing impact: embedding jobs hitting 5xx and timeouts. Ingress latency spike: p95 gen latency 2.4s -> 9.7s. Throughput dropped 42%. Affected customers: internal test tenants + three paying customers with batch embedding windows. Luis - any support tickets?

Luis (Support): yep, flagged two customers on pager. One enterprise (acme-corp) reporting >50% job failures on recent batch run. Escalation ticket created INC-4019. Customer impact: delayed processing, some retries causing duplicate downstream work.

Olivia Chen: immediate mitigations I want to try in parallel: 1) throttle non-prod/low-priority pools to free GPUs; 2) temporarily lower autoscaler cooldown & raise maxReplicas if cloud allows; 3) cordon + drain flaky nodes and force driver fallback on new nodes with different driver package. Suggestions?

Kai (Platform Eng): agree. prefer 1 + 3. We should avoid increasing maxReplicas until root cause clear — if driver is unstable we'll blow costs and still fail. For (3) I can push a conservative driver rollback to 525.x that was stable last week. Plan: taint nodes:```
kubectl taint nodes node-abc critical-driver-fail=true:NoSchedule
kubectl drain node-abc --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data
```
Then patch DaemonSet to use driver-image: `driver:525.14-stable` and rollout.

Maya Patel: prepared a quick rollout command:```
kubectl set image daemonset/gpu-driver driver-image=gcr.io/redwood/driver:525.14-stable -n infra
kubectl rollout status daemonset/gpu-driver -n infra --timeout=10m
```
If we can get driver pods stable on 5 nodes, autoscaler should be able to register them.

Jamal Singh: adding to that, we have autoscaler errors: "maxNodeCreationRateExceeded" and cloud provider rate limits. Recommend reducing scaleback for non-critical jobs and draining low-priority pods to make room. I can patch the scale policy quickly:```
# increase nodeGroup max temporarily
gcloud compute instance-groups managed set-autoscaling gpu-ig --max-num-replicas 60 --region europe-west3
```
(If cloud API allows).

Evan (ML Infra): while Kai rolls driver, I'm going to flip low-priority label on background embedding jobs so they get preempted:```
kubectl label namespace nonprod priority=low --overwrite
# eviction policy picks up priority label
```
This should free ~6 GPUs worth of capacity within 2 minutes.

OpsBot: NOTE: rate-limit change applied to /v1/embeddings for org:free-tier -> reduced qps by 60% to protect capacity.

Olivia Chen: status update 22:20 UTC: driver rollback started on 3 nodes, draining one noisy node. Queue stabilized a bit but still high: length 11.2k -> 9.6k (good). Throttle rate down to 54%.

Maya Patel: logs show Xid errors decreasing on nodes with rolled-back driver. New nodes register: pool size reported +3. Still seeing intermittent OOMs on long sequences — likely app memory configs too high. Suggest we also cap per-request token window for embeddings: set max_seq_len=4096 temporarily.

Jamal Singh: applied temporary policy: `max_seq_len=4096` for embedding-service via feature flag. patch:```
PATCH /config/features/embedding-service
{ "max_seq_len": 4096 }
```
Effect: immediate drop in memory blowups.

Luis (Support): told acme-corp we'll retry their batch and waive compute fees for the window. They appreciate the proactive communication.

Olivia Chen: still one problematic node that keeps re-registering then flapping. I'm going to cordon it and set it for postmortem analysis. `kubectl cordon node-flap-17` -> cordoned.

Kai (Platform Eng): rolling out driver-image to remaining nodes; monitoring GPU health checks. Also raising console alert thresholds to avoid false SLAs firing while we stabilize.

Evan (ML Infra): metrics: queue down to 6.1k, throttle 18%, errors trending down to baseline. Autoscaler happy: desiredReplicas=30, currentReplicas=30. Cloud queued 6 pending nodes, all registered.

Olivia Chen: customer impact: degraded for ~45min. Primary impact on large batch embeds (throughput and retries). Internal log: incident severity P2 (SLA degradation, not full outage).

OpsBot: INCIDENT UPDATE: reduced severity to P3 (mitigated) at 22:52 UTC. Root cause suspected: driver regression + combination of high memory requests -> OOM cascade -> node flaps -> autoscaler hitting rate limits.

Jamal Singh: next steps: 1) full driver rollback across prod pool overnight; 2) coordinate with release team to hold driver rollouts until QA adds kernel module stress test; 3) create autoscaler safety throttle: if node flaps >3 in 10m, pause scale-up to avoid churn. I'll open followups.

Maya Patel: adding eval checklist for memory safety: reject requests > 4096 tokens by default, add per-container memory reservation for embedding worker to avoid OOM kill.

Olivia Chen: oncall handover: handing to Jamal for night coverage at 23:00 UTC. Notes: flaky node cordoned, rollback progressing, support notified, customers briefed, followups: INC-4019 (customer), ENG-4102 (driver rollback postmortem), SRE-4110 (autoscaler safety). Ping if anything spikes.

Jamal Singh: taking over. acknowledged. thanks for triage. I will monitor overnight and start follow-ups in the morning. :thumbsup:
